data.long_meaning: The name Ahida is derived from the Arabic root 'Ahd' which means 'contract', 'covenant', or 'promise'. In Islamic context, the name Ahida signifies the promise or covenant made by Allah to His prophets and messengers. This name is considered a spiritual and meaningful name for a baby girl in Islamic culture. The name Ahida carries the meaning “Given by Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ahida usually hope their child will grow to embody given by allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah' mentions a Berber ruler named Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, also known as Ahmad al-Watiq Billah (the Just) or Ahida ibn Ibrahim. He ruled the Maghrib (North Africa) from Fez around 1356-1358.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes him as a learned man and a patron of scholars. He extended the boundaries of the Marinid empire and is known for his justice and fairness.

historical_references.reference: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ahidas was a prominent Sufi master in the 15th century in the city of Tlemcen, Algeria. He was a disciple of the famous Sufi master, Ibn Ata Allah of Rabat. Ahida is known for his teachings on love and self-annihilation in the path of God.
historical_references.context: Ahida's teachings have been influential among Sufis in North Africa and beyond.
